\]

\[\begin{equation}
\tag{4.1}
\forall x \\mathbb{R}, u \[0,1]: u \leq F(x) \iff F^{-1}(u) \leq x
\end{equation}\]
right-continuity \(F\). also note \(F\) bijective, inverse function identical generalised inverse \((0,1]\).Theorem 4.1  Let \(F\colon \mathbb{R} \rightarrow [0, 1]\) distribution function, \(U \sim U[0, 1]\) \(Y = F^{-1}(U)\). \(Y\) distribution function \(F\).Proof. (4.1) obtain
\[
\mathbb{P}(Y \leq x) = \mathbb{P}(F^{-1}(U) \leq x) = \mathbb{P}(U \leq F(x)) = F(x),
\]
last equality follows \(U \sim U[0, 1]\).theorem says random variable \(U \sim U[0, 1]\) want get \(Y \sim F\), can use \(F^{-1}(U)\).     0  & \text{otherwise.}
   \end{cases}
\]distribution function \(y \geq 0\) given 
\[\begin{align*}
F(y \mid \lambda) &= \int_0^y \lambda e^{-\lambda t}\,dt \\
& =  1 - e^{-\lambda y}.
\end{align*}\]
Finally, inverse function \((0,1)\) given 
\[
F^{-1}(y \mid \lambda) = -\frac{1}{\lambda}\log(1-y).  
\]
Therefore, \(U \sim U[0, 1]\), follows \(-\frac{1}{\lambda}\log(1-U) \sim \hbox{Exp}(\lambda)\).R code generates plot show (\(\lambda = 0.5\)). can plot CDF one parameter distributions straightforwardly. can think theorem allowing us sample point y-axis computing quantile corresponds .Example 4.2  Suppose want generate samples Cauchy distribution location 0 scale 1. density function
\[

\]
plot function shown .
use inverse transform method, first need find CDF:
\[
F(x) = \int_{-\infty}^x \frac{1}{\pi(1+t^2)}dt
\]
Letting \(t = \tan \theta\), can write \(dt = \sec^2(\theta)d\theta\). integral becomes
\[

\]
\(1 + \tan^2(\theta) = \sec^2(\theta)\), can write integral 
\[

\[

\]

squared.exponential.covariance <- function(x1, x2, alpha, ell) {
